root_cause.text: In `net/netfilter/nfnetlink_log.c`, the message size calculation for the `NLMSG_DONE` terminator used `nla_total_size(sizeof(struct nfgenmsg))` instead of `nlmsg_total_size(...)`, so the nfnetlink_log code undercounted the required netlink header space and could build an oversized skb, triggering a WARN and message drop.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `+ nla_total_size(sizeof(struct nfgenmsg)); /* NLMSG_DONE */` to `+ nlmsg_total_size(sizeof(struct nfgenmsg)); /* NLMSG_DONE */`, and the commit message explicitly says “NLMSG_DONE needs to account for the netlink header size, not just the attribute size.”

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet shows the exact size-accounting logic for the nfnetlink_log skb allocation and the fix for the root cause. The old bug was undercounting the trailing NLMSG_DONE/header space; the patched code now adds it explicitly: `+ nla_total_size(sizeof(struct nfgenmsg)); /* NLMSG_DONE */`. It also corrects the flush threshold by removing the extra subtraction: `if (inst->skb && size > skb_tailroom(inst->skb))`, replacing the prior `size > skb_tailroom(inst->skb) - sizeof(struct nfgenmsg)`.
